Question: No common point of line \(l\) and circle \(O\) is known. To prove that \(l\) is tangent to circle \(O\), the usual approach is to

Choices.A: Draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through the center \(O\), and prove that the length of the perpendicular segment equals the radius
Choices.B: Join \(O\) to any point on \(l\), and prove that the resulting segment is perpendicular to \(l\)
Choices.C: Prove that \(l\) passes through the center \(O\)

Solution: When no common point is known, use the approach “draw a perpendicular and prove its length equals the radius”: Draw \(OD\perp l\), then prove \(OD=r\). Thus \(d=r\), so the line is tangent to the circle.
